recent.title: US Conference Board consumer confidence (Oct)
recent.note: Beat: 91.7 vs 81.2 fcst (Sep revised up to 84.2) — biggest beat since May 2025; households catching up to the data as gasoline prices eased, but still on the long-term downtrend. Conference Board, Oct 27.

recent.title: US new home sales (Sep)
recent.note: Beat: 676K vs 660K fcst, though down from 680K Aug and 5.3% y/y — demand steadier than feared. Census/HUD, Oct 27.

recent.title: US house price indexes (Aug)
recent.note: Beat: +0.3% m/m vs 0.1% fcst (FHFA); Case-Shiller 20-city +2.7% y/y — housing wealth firm into the FOMC. FHFA / S&P Cotality, Oct 27.

recent.title: US durable goods orders (Sep)
recent.actual: +1.8% m/m ($345.4bn; vs 0.6% fcst; Aug rev. to +0.1%)
recent.note: Beat: +1.8% vs 0.6% fcst (WSJ consensus +1.7%) — nondefense aircraft +28.4% led, but ex-transport +0.5% and core cap goods ex-aircraft +0.5% both firmer; August revised up from flat. Census advance report, Oct 27.

recent.title: Dallas Fed manufacturing index (Oct)
recent.note: Beat: 13.4 vs 7.0 fcst (Sep 9.8) — headline strong, internals split: new orders collapsed to 9.3 from 30.7, production eased to 15.8, prices paid rose to 55.3, six-month outlook jumped to 38.1. Mixed signal, not a clean growth beat.

recent.title: Chicago Fed National Activity Index (Sep)
recent.note: Beat: +0.07 vs -0.10 fcst (Aug revised to -0.08 from -0.04); MA3 +0.03 (Aug +0.01) — just above trend into the FOMC; low-impact print, no dollar reaction.

recent.title: Eurozone M3 money supply y/y (Sep)
recent.note: Small beat: M3 held at 3.5% y/y vs 3.4% expected (prev 3.5%) — credit still expanding into Thursday's ECB hold.

recent.title: German Ifo business climate (Oct)
recent.note: Small beat: sixth straight rise, highest since May 2023; expectations 91.6 drove it (most optimistic in 4.5+ years) while current conditions 88.8 softened; EUR/USD +0.1% to ~1.1212 after the print.

recent.title: Belgian NBB business climate (Oct)
recent.note: Beat: -9.8 vs -11.8 fcst (Sep -12.1) — highest since January; mfg -9.2, building -8.3 improved; trade -13.2 worsened.

recent.title: Eurozone flash PMIs (Oct)
recent.actual: Comp 51.9 (fcst 52.7, Sep 53.1) — slowest in 4 months; Mfg 52.4 (52.9); Svc 51.7 (53.0)
recent.note: Miss: composite 51.9 vs 52.7 expected — slowest expansion in 4 months; France back in contraction (48.4) and rising energy-driven input costs (Reuters, Oct 23).

recent.title: Germany flash PMIs (Oct)
recent.actual: Comp 52.8 (vs 53.3 fcst, Sep 53.8); Mfg 54.2 (vs 53.5) beat; Svc 51.7 (vs 52.6)
recent.note: Mild composite miss (52.8 vs 53.3) though manufacturing beat (54.2); services the drag (Reuters, Oct 23).

recent.title: France flash PMIs (Oct)
recent.actual: Comp 48.9 (vs 50.5 fcst, Sep 51.1); Mfg 49.3; Svc 48.4 — back in contraction
recent.note: Back in contraction: 48.9 vs 50.5 expected as political/fiscal turmoil bites — the softest EZ read (Reuters, Oct 23).

recent.title: BRC shop price index y/y (Oct)
recent.note: Beat: fastest shop-price rise since Feb 2024 — food 2.9% (Sep 2.5%), non-food 1.7% (Sep 0.8%); retailers passing on energy, transport and employment costs into Wednesday's Budget.

recent.title: CBI realized sales (Oct)
recent.note: Big beat: slowest retail fall since Apr 2025; orders -36 (vs -62 Sep); sterling eased anyway on pre-Budget positioning ($1.3348).

recent.title: UK flash PMIs (Oct)
recent.actual: Comp 53.1 (vs 51.8 fcst, Sep 52.0) — strongest since Feb; Mfg 52.8; Svc 53.1
recent.note: Beat: 53.1 vs 51.8 expected, strongest since February — demand resilience alongside the BoE repricing (Reuters, Oct 23).

recent.title: UK retail sales m/m (Sep)
recent.actual: -0.4% m/m (vs -0.1% fcst; Aug rev. up to +0.7%)
recent.note: Miss: -0.4% vs -0.1% expected — warm weather hit clothing and supermarkets; Aug revised up to +0.7% (ONS/Reuters, Oct 23).

recent.title: CBI industrial order expectations (Oct)
recent.note: Miss: order-books balance fell to -32 vs -20 fcst (from -9 in September) — UK industrial gloom deepens; quarterly output outlook steadied. GBP held near the 1-month high — the miss was swamped by the CPI-driven BoE repricing (Reuters, Oct 22).

recent.title: GfK consumer confidence (Oct)
recent.note: Big miss: -24 vs -14 consensus — 11-pt drop, sharpest fall since the 2016 Brexit referendum (outside the pandemic); budget-anxiety sentiment ahead of the Oct 28 budget.

recent.title: Japan services PPI y/y (Sep)
recent.note: Inline: services PPI held at 3.7% y/y; ex-international-transportation eased to 2.9% from 3.2% — pipeline pressure steady, not accelerating, into Friday's BoJ decision.

recent.title: Japan flash PMIs (Oct)
recent.note: Manufacturing 53.3 (Sep 54.1) — 7-month low, miss vs 54.5 expected; services 52.0 (51.3) beat; composite 52.3 unchanged (19th straight expansion).

recent.title: Japan national core CPI y/y (Sep)
recent.note: Inline: 2.1% vs 2.1% consensus (Aug 1.7%) — first print above the BoJ's 2% target in nine months; core-core 2.4% (vs 1.9%) firms the case for a December hike.

recent.title: Japan trade balance (Sep)
recent.note: Miss: deficit nearly 3x forecast (-¥536.6bn vs -¥181bn); exports +16.7% y/y missed +20.1% exp — 5th straight monthly deficit; mineral-fuel import values +39.4% y/y.

recent.title: Japan tertiary industry activity m/m (Aug)
recent.note: Beat: -0.1% m/m vs -0.3% expected (prior +0.4%) — services held up; industrial production still the weak link.

recent.title: Japan revised industrial production (Aug)
recent.note: Revision deeper than prelim — second straight contraction, steepest since January.

recent.title: Swiss PPI m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Miss vs 0.6% fcst — disinflation intact; December SNB cut risk on the table.

recent.title: China loan prime rates (Oct)
recent.note: Inline: PBoC held LPR for the 17th straight month — neutral for the China-demand read.

recent.title: China Q3 GDP y/y (AUD demand read)
recent.note: Retail +1.1% the standout (2x fc); two-speed beat — factories lead, property -20.6% YTD. AUD best G10 performer.

recent.title: Australia jobs (Sep)
recent.note: Big miss: -39.3K jobs, unemployment 4.7% — five-year high, above RBA's 4.5% Q4 forecast.

recent.title: China trade balance (Sep)
recent.note: China exports +36.3% y/y vs 25.5% fcst — demand read for the Aussie.

recent.title: China CPI y/y (Sep)
recent.note: Soft China CPI (0.9% vs 1.0% fcst) — soft demand read for Australia's key customer; PPI +5.0% y/y.

recent.title: Canada retail sales m/m (Aug)
recent.note: A tenth light: +1.2% vs +1.3% fcst (Jul -0.7%); ex-autos +1.2% beat vs +1.0%; Sep advance +0.7% — essentially inline, loonie unmoved near 1.40.

recent.title: Canada IPPI m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Beat: +2.0% m/m vs 0.7% fcst (Aug rev. to +1.2%) — +14.5% y/y, 24th straight annual gain; upstream pressure supports the hawkish BoC repricing.

recent.title: Canada raw materials price index m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Big beat: +4.8% m/m vs 0.1% fcst (prev 3.1%) — +27.0% y/y; raw-material costs surging alongside the IPPI beat.

recent.title: Canada new housing price index m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Slight miss: -0.2% m/m vs -0.1% consensus — second straight soft month; Toronto and Oshawa steepest annual declines (-4.9% y/y). Shelter drag continues into the BoC's Oct 28 deliberation.

recent.title: Canada CPI y/y (Sep)
recent.note: Mild miss: 3.1% vs 3.2% Reuters consensus (prev 3.0%) — keeps October-28 a ~1-in-4 maybe after the -68.3K jobs miss.

recent.title: Canada foreign securities purchases (Aug)
recent.note: Big miss: first monthly divestment of 2026; record C$17.5B federal-debt cut.

recent.title: NZ CPI (Q3) q/q + y/y
recent.note: Soft miss on both measures — 0.7% q/q vs 0.8% fcst (prev 1.5%), 3.7% y/y vs 3.8% (from 4.1%; RBNZ had projected 3.9%) — but still above the 1–3% target; NZD dipped to $0.5692; Oct-28 hike stayed ~98% priced (Reuters, Oct 22).

recent.title: Global Dairy Trade Event 414
recent.note: Beat: powder-led firm — WMP +4.4% to $3,760/t, SMP +3.4% — positive terms-of-trade read into the Oct-28 RBNZ.

recent.title: NZ trade balance (Sep)
recent.note: Miss: NZ$1.97B deficit vs NZ$0.78B fcst — fuel import prices +96% y/y did the damage, not volumes.

recent.title: NZ food price index m/m (Sep)
recent.note: Food prices flat vs +0.3% prior — softens the near-term inflation pulse into Oct 28.

recent.title: NZ BusinessNZ manufacturing PMI (Sep)
recent.note: 56.5 vs 53.1 prior — strongest since 2021; 15th straight expansion; employment back growing.
